findings.detail: The before and after contracts differ only by the inserted 'Reporting clarifications (review T2/T4/T5)' section, placed after the unique N1/N2 sentence. The specification, assumptions, checker rules, metric definitions, exclusions (K5, C1-C4, F1-F8, HR ERRs unknown, rule 3.05), verdict and readiness meaning, and candidate status are textually unchanged. The functional artifacts are declared unchanged, and the supplied source is consistent with the documented behavior.

This clarification is accurate. close_epoch(lastc, False, 'terminated_unjudgeable_dut_output') sets closed_at to lastc, and the pending_at_unjudgeable_row record also carries cycle lastc. The termination path requires that pe is empty, and _validate puts a non-contiguous cycle into pe, so lastc is c-1 on this path. termination_boundary is S['term'], which equals c. On the first row, or before any reset, mode is pre_reset, so close_epoch returns without emitting a record. The text is also scoped to 'the epoch closed', which matches the existing statement that nothing is reflushed when the epoch is suspended or dead. T2 is fulfilled.

The core statement is accurate. rows_beyond_input_boundary is computed as nrows - total_rows. total_rows is incremented only after validation passes and before the row is processed. A row that fails validation or terminates on undefined DUT control output therefore breaks before the increment and is counted. A row where an environment violation is detected during processing is counted as processed. One case is not covered: with invalid limits, nrows = len(rows) and processed is 0, so the field equals all rows while neither input_validity_boundary nor termination_boundary is set. The phrase 'applies at either boundary' could be read as exhaustive. This is nonblocking; an optional note could cover the invalid_limits case. T4 is fulfilled as a documentation clarification and leaves the field name and computation unchanged.

The filter description matches the code: TAG_CLAUSE.get(u['item']) == k, and the listed exclusions are correct. However, same_edge_response_after_abort records (K13) are never carried in history tags. They are emitted directly by unr in the per-row K13 branch, not by any flush. The list of contributing flushes therefore omits the only source of K13 unknown_tag_records. The governing sentence ('counts only entries in the unresolved list whose item is one of the classified tag kinds') still makes the metric correct. This is nonblocking; an optional note could add 'and the direct per-row K13 same-edge record'. T5 is fulfilled. The text states the metric is not the total of unresolved diagnostics, not a clause status and not coverage.

limitations: This is a static, read-only documentation review of the supplied packet only. No code was executed and no traces were re-decoded for this call.
This review judges only whether the contract addendum accurately documents existing behavior for T2, T4 and T5. The prior code review and the full 158-case evidence remain separately authoritative.
This opinion is not certification or whole-IP proof. K5, C1-C4 and F1-F8 remain excluded or unproved. Timeout and cancellation bounds, both_interfaces_pending and rule 3.05 sub-row reset remain open.
This opinion does not freeze, register or authorize any replay, and does not authorize B or C.
